title: Endangered species in Nepal
notes: [Remember] IUCN ladder: Extinct → Critically Endangered (CR) → Endangered (EN) → Vulnerable (VU) → Near Threatened → Least Concern; threatened = CR + EN + VU only.
[Remember] Endangered mammals of Nepal: Bengal tiger, one-horned rhinoceros, snow leopard, red panda, hispid hare; birds: Bengal florican, vultures; reptiles: gharial, elongated tortoise.
[Understand] Why endangered: HIPPCO drivers — habitat loss and fragmentation, poaching and illegal trade, human–wildlife conflict, invasive species, pollution, climate pressure on Himalayan habitat.
[Understand] Where protected: Chitwan and Bardia (tiger, rhino, gharial, florican), Sagarmatha and Langtang (snow leopard, red panda), Koshi Tappu (wild buffalo, migratory birds).

[Apply] Strategy table — in-situ (national parks, reserves, conservation areas, buffer zones, corridors, anti-poaching) vs ex-situ (Central Zoo, breeding centres, seed/gene banks) with one species matched to each.
[Analyze/Evaluate] Success story: rhino rebound in Chitwan through in-situ protection plus community buffer zones; ongoing task: vulture recovery via diclofenac ban and vulture restaurants.
[Create] NEB answer frame: IUCN ladder → five Nepali endangered species with habitat → HIPPCO causes → in-situ/ex-situ strategies → rhino-success conclusion.
confusion: Threatened = CR + EN + VU only; Near Threatened and Least Concern are NOT threatened categories.
Endangered (EN) is one step safer than Critically Endangered (CR) — keep the ladder order exact.
A national park is stricter than a conservation area; a zoo is ex-situ, not in-situ.
Listing a species is not protection — name the strategy (buffer zone, anti-poaching, corridor) with it.
bounds: Covers only: endangered species in nepal (within Conservation Biology).
Out of scope here: topics of neighbouring units in Biology — don't mix them.
State the limit / condition where a formula or rule stops being valid before applying it.
practice: Write the IUCN ladder CR → EN → VU → NT → LC from memory with one Nepali species each for CR/EN/VU.
Expand HIPPCO with one Nepal-specific cause per letter.
Match five species to their protected area on a blank Nepal outline.
universalFacts: IUCN Red List categories are global standards; Nepal's protected-area network is the main in-situ answer.
Tiger, rhino and snow leopard are the three most-asked Nepali endangered mammals.
HIPPCO is the examiner's favourite acronym for 'causes of extinction' questions.
examples: One-horned rhinoceros rebound in Chitwan through anti-poaching and buffer-zone management.
Snow leopard protected across Sagarmatha and Langtang with livestock-insurance schemes.
Vulture recovery through the diclofenac ban and community vulture restaurants.
practiceQuestions: Write the IUCN threatened categories with one Nepali species for each. (3)

summary: Endangered species in Nepal: IUCN ladder, tiger–rhino–snow leopard–red panda–gharial with habitats, HIPPCO causes, in-situ and ex-situ strategies, Chitwan rhino success.
